high.title: [Bond Market - Weekly] Back-to-Back Hikes, Terminal Rate in Focus as July BOK Meeting Looms
high.summary:
A Bank of Korea rate hike at the July 16 Monetary Policy Board meeting is now widely considered a foregone conclusion, which would mark the BOK's first tightening move in approximately three and a half years since January 2023. The bond market is bracing for elevated volatility this week (July 13–16) as investors shift focus beyond the near-certain hike toward whether the BOK will signal the possibility of consecutive rate increases and where the terminal rate may ultimately land.

**Why it matters:** For Korean government bond (KTB) investors, the critical variable is no longer the July decision itself but the forward guidance embedded in the BOK's statement and Governor remarks. If the BOK opens the door to back-to-back hikes, short-end yields (2Y, 3Y) could reprice sharply higher, steepening the curve or triggering a broad sell-off across tenors. Duration positioning is particularly vulnerable here. Bond managers should watch closely for any dissenting votes or changes in the MPC's growth-inflation language. A hawkish surprise could also provide renewed upward pressure on KRW through rate-differential dynamics.

high.title: [FX-Weekly] Won Eyes BOK Meeting, SK Hynix Dollar Inflows, Forward Sales
high.summary:
The KRW/USD exchange rate closed below the psychologically significant 1,500 won level last week for the first time in roughly one and a half months, opening up further downside for the dollar (i.e., potential KRW appreciation). This week's FX market (July 13–17) is expected to be shaped by a confluence of supply-demand factors: the BOK's Monetary Policy Board meeting on July 16, dollar supply flows from SK Hynix (likely repatriating export revenues), and forward contract sales from heavy industry exporters. On the risk side, renewed U.S.-Iran military confrontation introduces a geopolitical wildcard that could trigger safe-haven dollar demand and reverse KRW gains.

**Why it matters:** The sub-1,500 break is technically significant and may trigger additional exporter dollar selling, reinforcing KRW strength in the near term. However, the geopolitical risk from U.S.-Iran tensions introduces asymmetric tail risk — a sudden escalation could rapidly push the pair back above 1,500. For FX traders, the BOK meeting is a dual catalyst: a hike alone is priced in, but hawkish forward guidance could amplify KRW strength through improved rate differentials. Watch SK Hynix-related flows and heavy industry forward sales as near-term supply-side anchors keeping USD/KRW contained.

high.title: [New York FX Market Weekly] Yen Short Positions Finally Unwinding as Japan's Repatriation Plan Remains Unclear
high.summary:
The New York foreign exchange market faces a high-volatility week as multiple macro catalysts converge. Speculative yen net short positions recorded their largest reduction in nearly two years, signaling a meaningful shift in positioning. However, the mechanism behind Japan's capital repatriation — particularly how the Government Pension Investment Fund (GPIF) will manage its overseas asset allocation — remains ambiguous, keeping the yen outlook uncertain. Key events this week include US CPI and PPI releases alongside Federal Reserve Governor Kevin Warsh's congressional testimony, both of which will be closely parsed for signals on the July FOMC meeting direction. Renewed geopolitical tensions in the Strait of Hormuz add an additional layer of risk-off pressure. For KRW traders, a strengthening yen and softer dollar momentum could provide modest support to Asian EM currencies including the won, while any hawkish Fed signals could reassert dollar strength. Korean government bond yields may also respond to US rate trajectory signals. Watch for CPI surprise risk and Warsh's tone on rate cuts as primary near-term drivers.

---

high.title: Dollar-Won Pares Losses on Trump's Iran Pressure, Trades Near 1,497 Won
high.summary: The USD/KRW exchange rate recovered from earlier lows during overnight New York trading, settling near the 1,497 level as two concurrent risk factors reinforced dollar strength against the won. First, President Trump's announcement of a resumption of a maritime blockade against Iran triggered a classic risk-off "dollar strength, won weakness" dynamic, as geopolitical escalation in the Gulf region typically prompts emerging market currency selling and a flight to dollar safety. Second, hawkish commentary from Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller — one of the most market-influential Fed voices — added further upward pressure on the dollar, reinforcing expectations that the Fed's tightening bias remains intact. For KRW traders, the 1,497 level is significant as it sits just below the psychologically critical 1,500 threshold. A breach of 1,500 could accelerate stop-loss driven won selling. Watch for BOK verbal or actual intervention signals if the rate approaches or breaks 1,500. This also has implications for Korean government bonds via imported inflation risks.

high.title: Waller Signals Support for Rate Hike This Month as Futures Market Betting Rises to 40%
high.summary: Fed Governor Christopher Waller has made explicitly hawkish remarks, indicating openness to a rate hike at the current month's FOMC meeting if core inflation data prints hot. According to the CME FedWatch Tool, futures markets briefly priced the probability of a July rate hike at approximately 40%, a notable jump that reflects growing market conviction around Fed tightening. The backdrop is compounded by surging international oil prices driven by the re-closure of the Strait of Hormuz. For KRW and Korean bond traders, this is a high-priority development: a Fed rate hike would widen the US-Korea interest rate differential further, increasing pressure on the BOK to respond or risk accelerated capital outflows and won depreciation. Korean government bond yields may face upward pressure as the market reprices the global rate path. The upcoming US CPI release this week is the key near-term catalyst — a hot print could rapidly push USD/KRW toward and potentially beyond 1,500. Fund managers should closely monitor both the data release and any BOK communications in response.

high.title: Trump Announces 'Iranian Blockade' Reinstatement, Signals 20% Toll on Hormuz Strait Traffic
high.summary:
U.S. President Donald Trump announced the reinstatement of blockade measures against Iranian waters, with signals of a potential 20% toll on traffic through the Strait of Hormuz — one of the world's most critical oil chokepoints. While article content is truncated, the geopolitical implications are significant for Korean markets. Korea is a major oil importer (~70% of crude via the Middle East), making it acutely sensitive to Hormuz disruptions. Any sustained rise in oil prices driven by this measure would widen Korea's trade deficit, exert depreciation pressure on the KRW, and stoke imported inflation — complicating the Bank of Korea's easing path. For bond traders, higher energy costs could delay rate cuts and push short-end yields higher. For FX desks, watch for KRW/USD upside pressure, particularly if this development coincides with the KOSPI's already severe selloff (down ~9% on the same day). This headline warrants close monitoring as an escalation could trigger risk-off flows out of emerging market assets, including Korean equities and KRW-denominated bonds.

medium.title: Korean Chip Stocks Test Limits of Rally Echoing Past Market Leaders
medium.summary:
The KOSPI experienced notable volatility, falling 5.35% to 7,246.79 on July 8 before partially recovering to 7,291.91 (+0.62%) on July 9. Bargain hunters are being pushed away by the sharp slide, with individual investors rotating out of equities and into bank deposits and ultra-short-term products, while recent market swings are driving inflows into absolute-return funds. This equity-to-deposit rotation is worth monitoring for KRW liquidity dynamics and its potential influence on domestic bond demand, though the direct FX or rates impact remains secondary to the BOK meeting this week.

medium.title: Foreigners' Top ETF Purchase is 'Inverse' — Reality is Derivative Arbitrage Paired Trading
medium.summary:
Foreign investors' largest ETF purchases in the Korean market are concentrated in inverse products, which on the surface suggests bearish positioning. However, the analysis clarifies this is largely a derivative arbitrage strategy — "paired trading" — driven by the rapid growth of single-stock leveraged ETFs that mechanically require inverse hedges. This dynamic creates an illusion of broad market bearishness while the underlying driver is structural rather than directional. For fund managers tracking capital flows and foreign investor sentiment in Korean equities, this distinction is important: net foreign positioning may be less bearish than headline ETF flow data implies. It also has modest implications for KOSPI volatility and KRW, as sustained foreign equity engagement — even via derivatives — limits the risk of abrupt capital outflow pressure on the won.

---

medium.title: South Korea's Tax Revenue to Exceed 500 Trillion Won for First Time Next Year — Total Spending to Rise Over 10%
medium.summary: South Korea's government is preparing a record-breaking budget for fiscal year 2027, with national tax revenue projected to surpass 500 trillion won (~$422 billion) for the first time in history and total expenditure exceeding 800 trillion won (~$676 billion). The fiscal expansion is being described as a "high-pressure economy" strategy, deliberately concentrating windfall revenues from the semiconductor super-cycle and AI-related growth into mega infrastructure and strategic investment projects, including an 800 trillion won "AI Investment Budget." This signals a significant shift toward proactive fiscal loosening. For KRW and KTB traders, this is worth monitoring: large-scale fiscal expansion could widen the fiscal deficit trajectory, adding supply pressure to the government bond market and potentially dampening BOK's flexibility to cut rates. However, stronger tax revenue underpinned by the semiconductor cycle may support KRW through improved current account dynamics. Watch for bond auction calendar updates and any BOK commentary on fiscal-monetary coordination.

medium.title: Government Prioritizes Fiscal Spending on Mega Projects, Vows 'Proactive Fiscal Policy' for Next Year
medium.summary: The South Korean government is undertaking its largest-ever spending restructuring, channeling resources toward mega national projects while establishing a new "Future Response Fund" to sterilize additional tax revenue. Key social commitments include creating over 300,000 youth jobs and priority allocation of new-type public rental housing. While primarily a domestic fiscal and social policy story, the scale of spending restructuring carries implications for KTB issuance volumes and the medium-term fiscal balance. Fund managers should note that a sustained "proactive fiscal policy" stance may create upward pressure on long-end KTB yields if bond supply increases meaningfully, and could complicate the BOK's rate path calculations heading into H2 2026.

medium.title: JMIC - Iran Maritime Blockade to Begin at 8 PM GMT on the 14th
medium.summary: The Joint Maritime Information Center (JMIC), representing a 47-nation coalition naval force, confirmed that the U.S. military's blockade of Iranian ports and coastal waters will take effect at 8 PM GMT on July 14th (4 PM Eastern Time). The blockade covers all Iranian ports and coastal areas. This is a direct market-moving development: Iran blockade enforcement raises the immediate risk of oil supply disruption via the Strait of Hormuz, which carries approximately 20% of global oil trade. For Korean markets specifically, South Korea is a major oil importer, meaning sustained oil price spikes translate directly into inflationary pressure, a wider current account deficit, and structural won weakness. Equity investors in Korean energy-intensive sectors should also remain cautious. This event is the primary geopolitical driver of the current USD/KRW upward move and warrants close monitoring as the blockade commences.

medium.title: Iranian Foreign Minister Mocks Trump's 'Toll' Declaration - '20% Is Too Much'
medium.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi responded sarcastically to Trump's proposal to charge service fees to ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz, writing on X that Iran — as the country ensuring safe passage — should be the one collecting compensation, and that Trump's proposed 20% toll is excessive. While delivered in a mocking tone, the comments signal Iran's intention to assert rival authority over Strait of Hormuz transit, raising the risk of confrontational incidents as the U.S. blockade takes effect. For KRW traders, escalating rhetoric increases the probability of a prolonged geopolitical standoff, supporting sustained oil price elevation and won weakness pressure. Any incidents involving vessels near Iranian waters could trigger sharp risk-off moves in Asian FX markets when Seoul opens.

medium.title: [Market Close] 'Black Monday' Despite Hynix ADR Success — KOSPI Crashes Below 7,000
medium.summary:
South Korea's KOSPI plunged 8.95% to close at 6,806.93 — a drop of 669.01 points — marking its worst single-session decline in recent memory and pushing the index below the psychologically critical 7,000 level for the first time in approximately two months. Semiconductor stocks led the selloff despite SK Hynix's successful ADR listing on a U.S. exchange. The circuit breaker was triggered during the session, reflecting the severity of the dislocation. For international fund managers, this scale of equity market decline has direct FX and fixed income implications: forced selling by foreign investors could drive KRW depreciation, while a flight to safety may temporarily support Korean government bond (KTB) prices. Watch for BOK commentary or emergency liquidity signals, as well as any coordinated government stabilization measures. The severity of this session increases the risk of near-term foreign capital outflows from Korean equities.

medium.title: KOSPI Plunges Nearly 9%, Crashes Below 7,000
medium.summary:
While equity index moves are generally outside this briefing's core focus, a KOSPI decline of nearly 9% — with the index crashing below the psychologically critical 7,000 level — carries significant cross-asset implications that demand attention. A shock of this magnitude typically triggers sharp risk-off positioning in Korean assets broadly, including accelerated KRW depreciation pressure as foreign investors unwind equity positions and repatriate capital, potential widening of Korean sovereign credit spreads, and elevated demand for BOK intervention in FX markets. Such a sell-off may also prompt emergency liquidity considerations from the Bank of Korea. **Note:** The article's full content was restricted (paywall/copyright block), so specific catalysts driving the decline — whether domestic policy shock, geopolitical trigger, or global contagion — cannot be confirmed. Traders should urgently seek confirmation of the underlying driver, as it will determine whether this is a short-term dislocation or the start of a sustained capital outflow episode. Monitor USD/KRW closely for potential spike above key resistance levels.
